column4: java.util.Random seeded with consecutive integers draws correlated first values: every M3 scenario drew a set and every JDK scenario a map, so the M3TreeMap views were never exercised; mix the seed (golden-ratio multiply) before new Random and print the scenario mix

column4: a one-shot comparator armed at an absolute call number fires during the owner's own construction (about 60-130 setup comparisons), so re-entrant cursors were never hit; arm it relative to the calls the setup made, and disarm a never-fired action before verifyInvariants (which compares keys and would run it inside its own walk)
column5: mutants RO-1, RO-5, RO-6, MU-3 survived the absolute arming and are killed by the relative arming; 19 'ordering' end states were verify-time artefacts

column4: a slot cursor's own remove must not go back through a key lookup: the lookup's comparator can clear the owner, miss the key, and the one modification of the clear then passes for the cursor's own erase; erase the returned slot directly (the donor's set-cursor shape)
column5: differential s2519/s2562 (M3TreeSet descending cursor, clearing comparator inside remove): the cursor walked released slots and returned null keys

column4: 'verifyInvariants throws ordering' after a re-entrant comparator is not by itself tree damage: verify compares keys, so an armed comparator runs inside it; re-run verify once the action is spent and compare with a JDK TreeMap copy before calling it a tree bug, and look for the neighbouring real damage (key removal erasing a released slot)
